sections.heading: Background and other versions
sections.wikitext:
Prince originally wrote "I Feel For You" and his hit single "[[I Wanna Be Your Lover]]" for musician [[Patrice Rushen]], but she turned down both songs.<ref>{{cite book| url= https://archive.org/details/princepurplereig0000wall | url-access= registration | page= [https://archive.org/details/princepurplereig0000wall/page/32 32] |title= Prince: Purple Reign |first= Mick| last= Wall| date= July 28, 2016 |publisher= Orion Publishing Group |via= Internet Archive}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1= McInnis |first1= C. Liegh|title=The Lyrics of Prince Rogers Nelson: A Literary Look at a Creative Musical Poet, Philosopher, and Storyteller |date=November 1, 2007 |publisher= Psychedelic Literature |isbn= 978-0965577502 |page= 177| edition= Third |chapter= Chapter 5: 'Laying a Foundation'}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-07 |title=5 Songs You Didn't Know Prince Wrote That Were Made Famous by Other Artists |url=https://americansongwriter.com/5-songs-you-didnt-know-prince-wrote-that-were-made-famous-by-other-artists/ |access-date=2022-08-01 |website=American Songwriter |language=en-US}}</ref> Prince subsequently recorded them for his eponymous second album, which was released in October 1979.<ref name="greatestcovers">{{cite book| url= https://books.google.com/books?id=hY-WAgAAQBAJ&pg=PA108 |title= 100 Greatest Cover Versions: The Ultimate Playlist|first=Robert|last=Webb|date=July 15, 2013| publisher= McNidder and Grace Limited|isbn= 9780857160577|via=Google Books}}</ref> For the song, Prince uses a [[falsetto]] vocal with the melody range between C<sub>3</sub> and D<sub>5</sub>.<ref>{{cite book |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=qXDoK4oZfsYC&pg=PA235| title= 'Just Another One of God's Gifts': Prince, African-American Masculinity, and the Sonic Legacy of the Eighties |date=January 1, 2008| isbn= 9781109120745 |via=Google Books}}</ref> 

[[The Pointer Sisters]] recorded the song in 1982 on their album ''[[So Excited!]]'',<ref name=greatestcovers/> and [[Rebbie Jackson]] recorded it for her 1984 debut album ''[[Centipede (album)|Centipede]]''.<ref>{{cite web| url= https://www.discogs.com/Rebbie-Jackson-Centipede/master/140100| website= Discogs.com| title= Rebbie Jackson – Centipede| date= 1984| access-date= November 22, 2019}}</ref> In 1993, [[Britney Spears]] and [[Justin Timberlake]] sang this song on ''[[The Mickey Mouse Club]]''.<ref>{{Cite magazine| url= https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/flashback-britney-justin-and-christina-on-the-mickey-mouse-club-232800/|title=Flashback: Britney, Justin and Christina on 'The Mickey Mouse Club' |date=January 22, 2015| magazine=[[Rolling Stone]].com| first= Andy| last= Greene| access-date= November 22, 2019}}</ref>

In October 2019, in honor of the 40th anniversary of the album ''[[Prince (album)|Prince]]'', the Prince Estate and Warner Records released a previously unheard solo acoustic demo recording of the song, with Prince also performing acoustic guitar. The track became available on streaming services and as a limited-run 7” vinyl single which sold out.<ref>{{cite web| url= https://store.prince.com/product/5QLPPR048/i-feel-for-you-acoustic-demo-7-exclusive-limited-edition?cp=103229_103233_103248| title= I Feel For You (Acoustic Demo) 7" Exclusive Limited Edition| website= prince.com| access-date= November 22, 2019}}</ref>
sections.text:
Prince originally wrote "I Feel For You" and his hit single "I Wanna Be Your Lover" for musician Patrice Rushen, but she turned down both songs. Prince subsequently recorded them for his eponymous second album, which was released in October 1979. For the song, Prince uses a falsetto vocal with the melody range between C<sub>3</sub> and D<sub>5</sub>. 

The Pointer Sisters recorded the song in 1982 on their album So Excited!, and Rebbie Jackson recorded it for her 1984 debut album Centipede. In 1993, Britney Spears and Justin Timberlake sang this song on The Mickey Mouse Club.

In October 2019, in honor of the 40th anniversary of the album Prince, the Prince Estate and Warner Records released a previously unheard solo acoustic demo recording of the song, with Prince also performing acoustic guitar. The track became available on streaming services and as a limited-run 7” vinyl single which sold out.

[[Chaka Khan]]'s version of "I Feel for You" featured a supporting cast including rapping from [[Melle Mel]] (of [[Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five]]); guitar, drum programming, bass guitar, keyboards and arrangement by Reggie Griffin; bass synthesizer and programming by [[The System (band)|The System]]'s David Frank using an [[Oberheim DSX]] [[Music sequencer|sequencer]], which was connected to his [[Minimoog]] via [[CV/gate|CV and gate]]; and [[chromatic harmonica]] playing by [[Stevie Wonder]]. The song also uses vocal [[Sampling (music)|samples]] from Wonder's song "[[Fingertips]]" (1963). The repetition of Khan's name by Melle Mel at the beginning of the song was a mistake made by producer [[Arif Mardin]], who then decided to keep it.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/templates/transcript/transcript.php?storyId=5061890|title=Arif Mardin: Tales from the Recording Studio |website=NPR.org |date=December 19, 2005 |access-date=March 29, 2014}}</ref>

This version of the song sold more than one million copies in the US and UK, helping to relaunch Khan's career and becoming her biggest hit as a solo artist. The song hit No. 1 on the ''[[Cashbox (magazine)|Cash Box]]'' singles chart and peaked at No. 3 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart from the weeks of November 24, 1984 to December 8, 1984.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/1984-11-24|title=Music: Top 100 Songs – Billboard Hot 100 Chart|date=January 2, 2013|magazine=Billboard|access-date=1 January 2018}}</ref> The song remained on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 for 26 weeks and became one of ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]''{{'}}s five biggest pop songs of the year for 1985. The single reached No. 1 on both the US [[Dance Club Songs|Hot Dance/Disco]]<ref>{{cite book |title= Hot Dance/Disco: 1974–2003|last=Whitburn |first=Joel |author-link=Joel Whitburn |year=2004 |publisher=Record Research |page=144}}</ref> and [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|Hot Black Singles]] charts in late 1984, remaining atop both for three weeks each.<ref>{{cite book |title= Top R&B/Hip-Hop Singles: 1942–2004| last= Whitburn |first= Joel |year=2004 |publisher=Record Research |page=321}}</ref> In addition, the song also reached No. 1 on the [[UK Singles Chart]], remaining there for three weeks from November 4–25, 1984.<ref name="British Hit Singles & Albums">{{cite book| first= David| last= Roberts| year= 2006| title= [[British Hit Singles & Albums]]| edition= 19th| publisher= Guinness World Records Limited | location= London| isbn= 1-904994-10-5| page= 442}}</ref> While touring with Prince in 1998 in support of her collaborative album, ''[[Come 2 My House]]'', Khan and Prince performed "I Feel for You" as a duet.

Khan's version of the song is written in the key of [[G-flat major|G{{flat}} major]] with a [[tempo]] of 125 beats per minute in [[Time signature|common time]].  Khan's vocals span from D{{flat}}<sub>4</sub> to A{{flat}}<sub>5</sub> in the song.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://songbpm.com/chaka-khan/i-feel-for-you|title=BPM for 'i feel for you' by chaka khan {{!}} songbpm.com|website=songbpm.com|access-date=2016-10-12}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtd.asp?ppn=MN0095541|title=Chaka Khan "I Feel for You" Sheet Music in G Major (transposable) – Download & Print|last=Prince|website=Musicnotes.com|date=December 12, 2011|access-date=2016-10-12}}</ref>

In 1985 at the 27th Annual Grammy Awards, the Chaka Khan version of "I Feel for You" won the Grammy for Best R&B Vocal Performance, Female.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chaka Khan |url=https://www.grammy.com/artists/chaka-khan/12106 |access-date=2023-08-06 |website=www.grammy.com}}</ref>

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
The first version of the [[music video]] for Khan's song featured her working in a club with female dancers. As [[Hip hop music|rap music]] and [[breakdancing]] were gaining popularity in mainstream pop culture at the time, the song was released and proved a success, so another version of the video, in an inner-city courtyard setting, was created. 

Director [[Little Witches|Jane Simpson]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Chaka Khan: I Feel for You |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8267316/?ref_=nm_flmg_t_18_dr |website=imdb.com |access-date=2023-05-26}}</ref> — who had graduated from [[UCLA]]'s film school and worked in animation before moving to work on commercials — was brought in as the director for what would be her first music video. Simpson and the production company who produced Chaka Khan’s video for the track had already been working on a video combining some of the early [[1980s in fashion|1980s day-glo fashions]] with breakdancing and [[rap]]. Simpson had already approached several designers who had rejected her concept before [[Norma Kamali]] agreed to let her clothing designs appear in the video, which was originally titled “Street Beat”, and shot in a studio mocked-up to look like the multi-racial hip hop club Radio-Tron in the MacArthur Park area in L.A. The choreographer was Joanne DiVito; break dancers appearing in the footage were [[Shabba Doo]], [[Michael Chambers|Boogaloo Shrimp]], Bruno "Pop N Taco" Falcon and Ana "Lollipop" Sánchez, all of whom also appeared in the movie ''[[Breakin']]''.<ref>{{cite web| url= http://www.myvideo.de/watch/3034573/I_feel_for_you |title=I feel for You Video  |website= Myvideo.de |date=July 2, 2013 |access-date=March 29, 2014}}</ref> To this pre-shot footage was added new footage of Chaka Khan and deejay [[Chris Taylor (music producer)|Chris "The Glove" Taylor]] spinning a hot pink-colored 12-inch single with “Chaka” printed on the label, as well as Khan standing near a [[Chain-link fencing|chain-link fence]] and other props, including graffiti-covered panels, on a studio soundstage.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://nightflight.com/i-feel-for-you-chaka-khans-1984-video-featured-breakdancing-rap-hip-hop-fashion/|title='I Feel For You': Chaka Khan's 1984 video featured breakdancing, rap & hip-hop fashion | website= NightFlight.com |date=July 10, 2017|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170710055052/http://nightflight.com/i-feel-for-you-chaka-khans-1984-video-featured-breakdancing-rap-hip-hop-fashion/ |accessdate= March 11, 2023|archive-date=July 10, 2017 }}</ref>

A remixed version of the video was later created to match the 12-inch vinyl version of the single.
sections.text:
The first version of the music video for Khan's song featured her working in a club with female dancers. As rap music and breakdancing were gaining popularity in mainstream pop culture at the time, the song was released and proved a success, so another version of the video, in an inner-city courtyard setting, was created. 

Director Jane Simpson — who had graduated from UCLA's film school and worked in animation before moving to work on commercials — was brought in as the director for what would be her first music video. Simpson and the production company who produced Chaka Khan’s video for the track had already been working on a video combining some of the early 1980s day-glo fashions with breakdancing and rap. Simpson had already approached several designers who had rejected her concept before Norma Kamali agreed to let her clothing designs appear in the video, which was originally titled “Street Beat”, and shot in a studio mocked-up to look like the multi-racial hip hop club Radio-Tron in the MacArthur Park area in L.A. The choreographer was Joanne DiVito; break dancers appearing in the footage were Shabba Doo, Boogaloo Shrimp, Bruno "Pop N Taco" Falcon and Ana "Lollipop" Sánchez, all of whom also appeared in the movie Breakin. To this pre-shot footage was added new footage of Chaka Khan and deejay Chris "The Glove" Taylor spinning a hot pink-colored 12-inch single with “Chaka” printed on the label, as well as Khan standing near a chain-link fence and other props, including graffiti-covered panels, on a studio soundstage.

A remixed version of the video was later created to match the 12-inch vinyl version of the single.
